newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares hold gains but Fed watch dulls trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares hold gains but Fed watch dulls trade.

text.p: Dutch shares ambled to a higher close on Tuesday after a day bereft of serious investor activity ahead of the key Federal Reserve meeting, which many believe could result in a rise in U.S. interest rates.
The index of leading shares remained in positive territory throughout the day, although a weaker start to Wall Street late in the Amsterdam session sapped some of the earlier strength.
The AEX still finished 2.30 points, or 0.41 percent higher at 563.97, below the intra-day high of 564.75.
"Things are basically on hold ahead of the meeting -- all we've got is a dealer market at the moment," one trader said.
Dealers said the market was braced for a 1/4 point rise in U.S. rates but a lingering possibility of more stringent credit tightening had left most players sidelined, taking few chances.
One of the few blue-chips to move significantly was chemical firm Akzo Nobel, which forged ahead after Monday's post-bourse announcement on positive trials of its Remeron antidepressant.
The company claimed the trials showed it to be more effective at combatting depression than the world's best-seller Prozac made by Eli Lilly of the United States.
Dealers said the news sparked some short-covering in the shares and some limited buying but also noted volume was light.
By the close Akzo Nobel was 5.90 guilders, or around three percent, higher at 198.90. Fellow chemicals company DSM also fared well, moving 3.00 guilders ahead to 168.00.
Electronics giant Philips continued Monday's run, topping the volume list and adding another 0.90 guilders to 60.60 after presentations to analysts were generally well received.
Elsewhere in the index there was little activity. Financials had a slack day with ABN AMRO ending 0.20 higher at 91.90 and ING up 0.10 at 52.20.
